Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via the cited source: DataReportal Digital 2025 (data to Jan 2025) reports 15.7% internet penetration (1.90m users), matching Code 2. But DataReportal's own Digital 2026 update (data to Oct 2025) revises this down to 13.2%, and World Bank/ITU official data (2022, most recent published) shows 12.1% — both would fall in Code 1 (<15%). The true figure sits right on the 15% boundary with conflicting recent estimates; left unchanged but flagged for human review rather than guessed.

Definition: Unique mobile subscriber penetration rate as a percentage of the total population. Measures the proportion of individuals who subscribe to a mobile service (not SIM cards, which can be multiple per person). Mobile phones are the primary device for internet access in Africa.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The variable specifically requires unique-subscriber penetration, not connections. The cited DataReportal figure (37.1%, 2025) is total mobile connections/SIMs, and the row's own comment already estimated unique subscribers at only 30-40% — inconsistent with the assigned Code 3 (40-54%). GSMA's Connectivity for Refugees country profile (2024, drawing on ~2022 data) gives unique mobile subscriber penetration of just 25.65%. Allowing for growth in connections since (37% to 48% by late 2025), true unique-subscriber penetration is most plausibly in the 25-39% range; revised down to Code 2.

Definition: The country's overall cybersecurity preparedness, based on the ITU Global Cybersecurity Index (GCI). Covers legal measures, technical measures, organisational measures, capacity development, and cooperation. Essential for trust in stored data and digital services.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original ITU PDF link is now dead (404), but the GCI 2024 score of 34.38 for South Sudan is corroborated by an independent data aggregator citing ITU as its source, and matches the ITU's own description of the 'Evolving' (Tier 4) band. Value Code 2 (GCI 20-39) confirmed.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Draft legislation or partial provisions in other laws
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct read of the cited source (published Dec 2025): the ICT minister states South Sudan has no Data Protection Act yet and a bill is planned for introduction in 2026, alongside the separately passed Cybercrime and Abuse of Computer Bill 2025. Supports Code 2 (no legislation yet, draft/planned).

Definition: Whether the country has established policies, regulations, and programmes supporting off-grid and distributed energy solutions (mini-grids, solar home systems). These are critical for extending ICT infrastructure to unserved areas beyond the central grid.
Value Name: Basic policy exists but limited implementation
Comments: Basic policy limited implementation; market assessment shows small private sector, high taxes on solar
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed: South Sudan has a National Electricity Policy (2013) and a draft National Electricity Bill (2015, passed by cabinet but never ratified), and the National Development Strategy 2018-2024 prioritises off-grid/renewable expansion, but implementation remains weak — no independent regulator, conflict-damaged rural mini-grids, and a small private off-grid sector facing high import taxes on solar equipment. Supports Code 2 (basic policy, limited implementation).

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed via direct read of the World Bank Pathways survey (2022 field data, published 2023): about 30% of urban households have electricity access versus ~1.7-2% of rural households, a gap of roughly 28 percentage points, which sits within the 21-40pp band (Code 3). Note that World Bank WDI modelled data shows a lower urban figure (19.1% in 2023), which would narrow the gap to ~17pp (Code 4); the directly-sourced survey figures used in the original entry are preferred and the score is confirmed.

Definition: The number and activity level of technology hubs, incubators, accelerators, and co-working spaces focused on technology and innovation. These provide physical infrastructure and support for tech entrepreneurship and skills development.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Original source (a 2021 tweet) is superseded and was not independently verifiable. The current AfriLabs directory lists three active member hubs in South Sudan (Konetahub, Ataka Hub, Junub Open Space), and at least two further active hubs exist outside that network (Scenius Hub, a Juba youth hub with 600+ members, and the University of Juba's UNIPOD, a $1.2m facility launched in 2023 with UNDP support). This is consistent with 3-9 hubs showing regular activity; revised up to Code 3.
